depends_on: The puppy's age: from about 6 months, FEDIAF allows a calcium minimum of 2.0 g/Mcal and a Ca:P maximum of 1.8; this check uses 2.5 and 1.6.
The breed: for Great Dane puppies FEDIAF prefers a calcium maximum of 1.6% DM, which is not applied here.
Whether the amount is added as an additive: FEDIAF's EU legal maximum applies only to that amount.
The form added: iron added as oxide or carbonate should not count toward the minimum.
The form added: copper added as oxide should not count toward the minimum.
Separate limits on the amount of selenium added (such as AAFCO's additive approval limit and FEDIAF's limit on organic selenium) are not checked: this checker has no input for added selenium.
AAFCO's limit on phosphorus from soluble sources is not checked.
The diet's fish content: AAFCO requires vitamin K for cats only above 25% fish in dry matter; this minimum applies to every diet.
Antimicrobial or anti-vitamin compounds: the standards require added biotin only then; this minimum applies to every diet.
How far the animal is from NRC's reference kitten or lactating queen: NRC states its per kg BW^0.67 values for that one animal.
This row is for foods with 12% moisture or less (FEDIAF uses 14%). For a wetter food, use the row for more than 12% moisture, whose minimum differs.
This row is for foods with more than 12% moisture (FEDIAF uses 14%). For a drier food, use the row for 12% moisture or less.

This row is for foods with 12% moisture or less; under this requirement its wet-food row has the same limits, so either gives the same result. Some standards set different copper, selenium and taurine limits by moisture or format, so using one value for both may not always be supported.

This row is for foods with more than 12% moisture; under this requirement its dry-food row has the same limits, so either gives the same result. Some standards set different copper, selenium and taurine limits by moisture or format, so using one value for both may not always be supported.

This row applies to foods of any moisture: there is no separate wet-food row per kg of body weight. Some standards set different copper, selenium and taurine limits by moisture or format, so using one value for both may not always be supported.
FEDIAF's wet-diet selenium values per kg BW^0.75 or BW^0.67 are not used.
The food's energy density: not entered, so AAFCO's minimums and maximums are not raised for a food below 4 kcal/g DM.
AAFCO compares this food on dry matter: its minimums and maximums here are AAFCO's dry-matter values per Mcal of this food.
